summary: LAST LIGHT 2.0 is an interactive 3D Junior Astronaut Training experience designed to introduce students to the challenges of human space exploration through immersive missions and hands-on learning. The experience follows four major stages: astronaut training on Earth, space launch and orbital ascent, establishing a lunar outpost, and developing a Martian outpost. Players explore mission scenarios involving spacecraft operations, life-support systems, resource management, habitats, and survival beyond Earth. By combining interactive gameplay, realistic 3D environments, educational narration, and mission-based progression, LAST LIGHT 2.0 aims to make complex STEM and space-science concepts engaging and accessible to young learners.

Project Description – LastLight (Astronaut’s Mission)

What does it do / How does it work?
LastLight is an interactive 3D browser-based space exploration and survival game. Players take on the role of an astronaut training for deep-space missions. They must manage critical resources (Oxygen, Stamina, Health, Hydration, Suit Battery, and Colony Power) while navigating different environments — from a training academy to a spacecraft, a lunar outpost, and a Martian colony. Players explore in first-person and third-person views, interact with objects, face environmental challenges like dust storms, and make decisions that affect the mission’s outcome.

What benefits does it have?

  • Makes space exploration and resource management engaging and fun for young learners
  • Teaches the importance of careful planning, resource conservation, and decision-making under pressure
  • Runs completely in the browser — no downloads or installations required
  • Accessible on both computers and mobile devices

What is the intended impact of the project?
The project aims to inspire the next generation of explorers, scientists, and engineers by giving them a hands-on, immersive experience of what it feels like to live and work in space. It encourages curiosity about space science, planetary exploration, and human survival beyond Earth.

Tools, coding languages, and software used:

  • HTML5 – structure of the game
  • CSS3 – styling and user interface
  • JavaScript – game logic and interactivity
  • Three.js – 3D graphics and rendering
  • GitHub – version control and source code hosting
  • Vercel – free and fast web hosting

How is your project creative?
Instead of a traditional 2D educational game, LastLight uses real-time 3D graphics to create an immersive astronaut experience. Players can freely explore different space environments, switch camera perspectives, and face realistic survival challenges. The combination of storytelling, resource management, and interactive 3D exploration makes learning about space feel like an adventure.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Making the game educational yet entertaining
  • Ensuring it works smoothly in a web browser without requiring powerful hardware
  • Designing simple and clear controls (WASD movement, mouse look, interactive keys)
  • Creating a meaningful progression from training → spacecraft → Moon → Mars
  • Keeping the entire project lightweight so it loads quickly and works on most devices
